‘Make seven lamps for it and set them up to shine toward the space in front of it. 🪔
‘Make its tongs and trays from pure gold. 🛠️
‘Use one talent of pure gold for the lampstand and all its accessories. ⚖️
‘Be careful to make everything according to the pattern I showed you on the mountain.’ 🏔️
‘Make the Tabernacle from ten curtains of finely twisted linen, with blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and designs of cherubim. A skilled craftsperson must make them. 🧵
‘Each curtain must be twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. Make all ten the same size. 📏
‘Join five curtains together as one set, and the other five together as another set. 🪡
‘Make blue loops along the edge of the curtain at the joining seam. Do the same along the edge of the outer curtain in the second set. 🔵
‘Make fifty loops on the edge of the curtain in each set, lining the loops up opposite one another. 🧵
‘Make fifty gold clasps and use them to connect the curtain sets, so the Tabernacle becomes one piece. ✨
‘Make eleven curtains of goat hair as a covering over the Tabernacle. 🐐
‘Each of these curtains must be thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. Make all eleven the same size. 📏
‘Join five curtains together as one set and six as another. Fold the sixth curtain over the front of the tent. 🪡
‘Make fifty loops along the outer edge of the curtain in each joined set. 🧵
‘Make fifty bronze clasps, put them through the loops, and join the curtains into one tent. 🟤
‘Let the extra half-curtain hang over the back of the Tabernacle. 🏕️
‘Let the extra cubit on each side hang down along the two sides of the Tabernacle to cover it. 📏
‘Make a covering for the tent from ram skins dyed red, with a covering of sea cow hides over that. 🐏
‘Make upright frames for the Tabernacle from acacia wood. 🪵
‘Each frame must be ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide. 📏
‘Make two matching tenons on each frame. Make every Tabernacle frame the same way. 🪚
‘Make twenty frames for the south side of the Tabernacle. 🔢
‘Make forty silver bases under those twenty frames—two bases under each frame, one for each tenon. 🪙
‘For the north side of the Tabernacle, make twenty frames, 🪵
‘and forty silver bases—two under each frame. 🪙
‘For the back of the Tabernacle on the west side, make six frames. 🧭
‘Make two extra frames for the back corners of the Tabernacle. 🪵
‘At the bottom, pair the corner frames. Join them all the way to the top with one ring. Make both corners the same way. 🔗
‘There will be eight frames in all, with sixteen silver bases—two bases under each frame. 🔢
‘Make crossbars from acacia wood: five for the frames on one side of the Tabernacle, 🪵
‘five for the frames on the other side, and five for the frames at the back on the west side. 🪵
‘The middle crossbar must run through the center of the frames from one end to the other. 📏
‘Cover the frames with gold, make gold rings to hold the crossbars, and cover the crossbars with gold too. ✨
‘Set up the Tabernacle according to the design shown to you on the mountain. 🏔️
‘Make a curtain of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen, with cherubim woven into it by a skilled craftsperson. 🧵
‘Hang it on four acacia posts covered with gold, with gold hooks and four silver bases. 🏛️
‘Hang the curtain under the clasps, then bring the Ark of the Covenant inside it. The curtain will separate the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place. 🏛️
‘Put the atonement cover on the Ark of the Covenant in the Most Holy Place. 📦
‘Put the table outside the curtain. Place the lampstand opposite it on the south side of the Tabernacle, and put the table on the north side. 🪔
‘Make an entrance screen for the Tent from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen. An embroiderer must make it. 🧵
‘Make five acacia posts for the screen and cover them with gold. Their hooks must be gold. Cast five bronze bases for them.’ 🏛️
‘Make the altar from acacia wood. It must be square—five cubits long, five cubits wide, and three cubits high. 🪵
‘Make a horn at each of its four corners as one piece with the altar, then cover the altar with bronze. 🟤
‘Make bronze pots for carrying away the ashes, along with shovels, bowls, meat forks, and fire pans. Make all its tools from bronze. 🛠️
‘Make a bronze grate like a net, with four bronze rings at its four corners. 🟤
‘Set the grate under the altar’s ledge, about halfway up the altar. 📐
‘Make carrying poles from acacia wood and cover them with bronze. 🪵
‘Put the poles through the rings on both sides of the altar so it can be carried. 🏛️
‘Build the altar hollow, with boards, following the design shown to you on the mountain. 🏔️
‘Make a courtyard for the Tabernacle. On the south side, hang a hundred cubits of fine twisted linen curtains. 🧵
‘There must be twenty posts with twenty bronze bases. The posts’ hooks and connecting bands must be silver. 🪙
‘Do the same on the north side: a hundred cubits of curtains, twenty posts, twenty bronze bases, and silver hooks and bands. 🧵
‘Across the west end, hang fifty cubits of curtains, with ten posts and ten bases. 📏
‘The east end must also be fifty cubits wide. 🧭
‘On one side of the entrance, hang fifteen cubits of curtains, with three posts and three bases. 🚪
‘On the other side, hang fifteen cubits too, with three posts and three bases. 🚪
‘For the courtyard entrance, make a twenty-cubit screen of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen, embroidered by a skilled craftsperson. Set it on four posts with four bases. 🧵
‘All the courtyard posts must have silver bands and silver hooks, with bronze bases. 🪙
‘The courtyard must be a hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and five cubits high. Its curtains must be fine twisted linen, and its bases bronze. 📐
‘Make all the Tabernacle tools and all its tent pegs—and the courtyard pegs—from bronze. 🛠️
‘Command Israel’s people to bring you pure pressed olive oil to keep the lamps burning continually. 🪔

‘In the Tent of Meeting, outside the curtain in front of the covenant tablets, Aaron and his sons must keep the lamps in order from evening until morning before Yahweh. This will be a lasting rule for Israel’s people through every generation.’ 🕯️
‘Bring your brother Aaron and his sons close to you from among Israel’s people, so they can serve me as priests: Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar. 👥
‘Make sacred garments for your brother Aaron—honorable and beautiful. ✨
‘Speak with every skilled craftsperson I’ve filled with wisdom. They must make Aaron’s garments to set him apart for priestly service to me. 🧵
‘Here are the garments they must make: a breastpiece, an ephod, a robe, a fitted tunic, a turban, and a sash. Make sacred garments for Aaron and his sons, so they can serve me as priests. 👘
‘Use gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine linen. 🪙
‘Make the ephod from gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen. A skilled craftsperson must make it. 🧵
‘Join two shoulder straps to its two ends so the ephod can be fastened together. 🔗
‘Make its skillfully woven waistband from the same materials as the ephod—gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and fine twisted linen. 🧵
‘Take two onyx stones and engrave on them the names of Israel’s sons. 💎
‘Put six names on one stone and the other six on the second, in the order the sons were born. 🔢
‘Have a stone engraver carve the names into the two stones like a seal. Set them in gold. 💎
‘Attach the two stones to the ephod’s shoulder straps as memorial stones for Israel’s people. Aaron will carry their names on his shoulders before Yahweh as a reminder. 🛡️
‘Make gold settings for the stones, 🪙
‘and two braided chains of pure gold. Attach the chains to the settings. ⛓️
‘Make a breastpiece for making decisions, skillfully woven like the ephod, from gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine twisted linen. 🧵
‘Make it square and double-layered, one span long and one span wide. 📐
‘Set four rows of stones in it. First row: ruby, topaz, and beryl. 💎
‘Second row: turquoise, sapphire, and emerald. 💎
‘Third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst. 💎
‘Fourth row: chrysolite, onyx, and jasper. Set all twelve stones in gold. 💎
‘The stones must match Israel’s twelve sons, one for each name, engraved like a seal for the twelve tribes. 🔢
‘Make braided chains for the breastpiece from pure gold. ⛓️
‘Make two gold rings and attach one to each end of the breastpiece. 💍
‘Thread the two gold chains through the rings at the breastpiece’s ends. 🔗
‘Attach the other ends of the chains to the two gold settings on the ephod’s front shoulder straps. 🪡
‘Make two more gold rings and attach them to the inner edge at the two ends of the breastpiece. 💍
‘Make two gold rings for the lower front of the ephod’s shoulder straps, close to where they join, just above its woven waistband. 💍
‘Tie the breastpiece’s rings to the ephod’s rings with blue cord, so it sits securely on the waistband and doesn’t swing away from the ephod. 🔵
‘Whenever Aaron enters the holy place, he’ll carry Israel’s names over his heart on the decision breastpiece, as a constant reminder before Yahweh. ❤️

‘Put the Urim and Thummim inside the decision breastpiece. They must be over Aaron’s heart whenever he comes before Yahweh. Aaron will carry Israel’s decisions over his heart before Yahweh continually. 📜
‘Make the ephod’s robe entirely blue. 🔵
‘Make a hole for the head in its center, with a woven collar around the opening so it won’t tear. 🧵
‘Around its hem, make pomegranates of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with gold bells placed between them. 🔔
‘Alternate a gold bell and a pomegranate all around the robe’s hem. 🔔
‘Aaron must wear it while serving. Its sound will be heard when he enters the holy place before Yahweh and when he comes out, so he won’t die. 🔔
‘Make a plate of pure gold, and engrave on it like a seal: “HOLY TO YAHWEH.” ✨
‘Attach it to a blue cord and fasten it to the front of the turban. 🔵
‘It must rest on Aaron’s forehead. Aaron will carry the guilt connected with Israel’s sacred gifts, so the gifts can be accepted before Yahweh. Keep the plate on his forehead at all times. 🕊️
‘Weave the tunic from fine linen. Make the turban from fine linen, and make the sash with embroidered work. 🧵
‘Make tunics, sashes, and headbands for Aaron’s sons too—honorable and beautiful. 👘
‘Put the garments on your brother Aaron and his sons. Anoint them, ordain them, and set them apart, so they can serve me as priests. 🙏
‘Make linen undergarments to cover their nakedness, from the waist down to the thighs. 🧵

‘Aaron and his sons must wear them whenever they enter the Tent of Meeting or approach the altar to serve in the holy place, so they don’t incur guilt and die. This is a lasting rule for Aaron and his descendants.’ 🕊️
Here’s how you’re to set them apart to serve me as priests: take one young bull and two rams with no defects. 🐂
Bring unleavened bread, oil-mixed unleavened cakes, and unleavened wafers brushed with oil. Make them from fine wheat flour. 🌾
Put the bread in one basket and bring it along with the bull and both rams. 🧺
Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Meeting Tent, then wash them with water. 💧
Take the garments and dress Aaron in the tunic, the ephod robe, the ephod, and the chest piece. Tie the ephod’s woven sash snug around him. 👘
Set the turban on his head and place the sacred crown on the turban. 👑
Then take the anointing oil, pour it over his head, and anoint him. 🫗
Bring his sons forward too, and put their tunics on them. 👕
Tie the belts on Aaron and his sons, and wrap their headbands in place. The priesthood belongs to them by a lasting rule. Set Aaron and his sons apart for this work. 🪢
Bring the bull to the Meeting Tent. Aaron and his sons must place their hands on the bull’s head. 🐂
Slaughter the bull before Yahweh at the entrance of the Meeting Tent. 🕊️
Put some bull’s blood on the altar’s horns with your finger, then pour all the remaining blood at the altar’s base. 🩸
Take all the fat covering the inner parts, the liver’s covering, both kidneys, and the fat on them; burn it all on the altar. 🔥
Burn the bull’s meat, hide, and dung outside the camp. This is the sin offering. 🕯️
Next, take one of the rams. Aaron and his sons must place their hands on its head. 🐏
Slaughter the ram, collect its blood, and splash it all around the altar. 🩸
Cut the ram into pieces. Wash its inner parts and legs, then arrange them with the pieces and its head. 🔪
Burn the whole ram on the altar. It’s a burnt offering to Yahweh, a pleasing smell and an offering made by fire to Yahweh. 🔥
Now take the other ram. Aaron and his sons must place their hands on its head too. 🐏
Slaughter this ram. Put some blood on Aaron’s right earlobe, on each son’s right earlobe, on each of their right thumbs, and on each of their right big toes. Then splash blood all around the altar. 🩸
Take some blood from the altar and some anointing oil, then sprinkle it on Aaron, his clothes, his sons, and their clothes. They and their garments are set apart for this service. 🕊️
Take the ram’s fat, its fat tail, the fat covering the inner parts, the liver covering, both kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh. This ram is for their ordination. 🐏
Also take one loaf, one oil-mixed cake, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread set before Yahweh. 🍞
Place all of it in Aaron’s hands and his sons’ hands, and have them lift it before Yahweh as a presentation offering. 🙌
Take the offering back from their hands and burn it on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. Its aroma is pleasing before Yahweh; it’s an offering made by fire to Yahweh. 🔥
Take the breast of the ram used for Aaron’s ordination and lift it before Yahweh as a presentation offering. That part is yours. 🤲
Set apart the breast and thigh of the presentation offering—the portions lifted up from the ordination ram, for Aaron and his sons. 🕊️
This is Aaron’s and his sons’ lasting share from Israel: it’s a presentation offering from Israel’s peace offerings, lifted up to Yahweh. 📜
Aaron’s sacred garments will pass to his sons after him. They’ll wear them when they’re anointed and set apart for service. 👘
The son who takes his place as priest must wear them for seven days whenever he enters the Meeting Tent to serve in the holy place. 🗓️
Take the ordination ram and cook its meat in a sacred place. 🍲
Aaron and his sons must eat the ram’s meat and the bread from the basket at the entrance of the Meeting Tent. 🍞
They must eat the food used to make atonement and set them apart. An outsider must not eat it, because it’s sacred. 🍽️
If any ordination meat or bread is still there by morning, burn what’s left. Don’t eat it; it’s sacred. 🔥
Carry out everything I commanded for Aaron and his sons. Their setting-apart ceremony lasts seven days. 🗓️
Each day, offer a bull as the sin offering for atonement. Cleanse the altar when you make atonement for it, then anoint it to set it apart. 🕊️
Make atonement for the altar for seven days and set it apart. Then it will be most holy; whatever touches it will be holy. ✨
Here’s what you must keep offering on the altar: two year-old lambs, every single day. 🐑
Offer one lamb in the morning and the other in the evening. 🌅
With the first lamb, offer a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with a quarter-hin of beaten oil, plus a quarter-hin of wine as a drink offering. 🫗
Offer the second lamb in the evening with the same grain and drink offerings as in the morning. It’s a pleasing aroma, an offering made by fire to Yahweh. 🌆
This will be a regular burnt offering for every generation, at the entrance of the Meeting Tent before Yahweh. That’s where I’ll meet you and speak with you. 🕊️
I’ll meet Israel there, and the place will be made holy by my glory. ✨
I’ll set apart the Meeting Tent and altar. I’ll also set apart Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests. 🙏
I’ll live among Israel and be their God. 🕊️
They’ll know I am Yahweh their God—the one who brought them out of Egypt so I could live among them. I am Yahweh their God. 🙌
Build an altar from acacia wood for burning incense. 🪵
Make it square: one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits tall. Its horns must be one piece with the altar. 📐
Cover the top, sides, and horns with pure gold, then add a gold border all the way around. ✨
Make two gold rings under the border, one on each of its two sides. They’ll hold the poles for carrying it. 💍
Make the carrying poles from acacia wood and cover them with gold. 🪵
Put the altar in front of the curtain beside the covenant chest, facing the atonement cover above the covenant. That’s where I’ll meet you. 🕊️
Every morning, Aaron must burn sweet incense on the altar while he gets the lamps ready. 🌅
When Aaron lights the lamps at dusk, he must burn incense again. Keep that incense offering going for every generation. 🌆
Don’t burn any unauthorized incense there, or bring a burnt, grain, or drink offering onto that altar. 🚫
Once each year, Aaron must make atonement on the altar’s horns with the blood of the atonement sin offering. Keep doing this through every generation. The altar is most holy to Yahweh. 🕊️
Yahweh spoke to Moses again: 📜
Whenever you count Israel, each person being counted must pay Yahweh a ransom for their life. Then no plague will strike them during the census. 🧮
Everyone counted must give half a shekel, measured by the sanctuary shekel—which equals twenty gerahs—as an offering to Yahweh. ⚖️
Everyone counted who is twenty years old or older must bring this offering to Yahweh. 🧑
When you give the offering to Yahweh to make atonement for your lives, the rich must not give extra and the poor must not give less than half a shekel. ⚖️
Collect this atonement money from Israel and use it for the Meeting Tent’s service. It will remind Israel before Yahweh that atonement was made for their lives. 🪙
Yahweh spoke to Moses again: 📜
Make a bronze basin with a bronze stand for washing. Set it between the Meeting Tent and the altar, then fill it with water. 🚰
Aaron and his sons must wash their hands and feet there. 💧
They must wash with water before going into the Meeting Tent or approaching the altar to serve and burn an offering to Yahweh. If they don’t, they’ll die. ⚠️
They must wash their hands and feet so they don’t die. This rule lasts for Aaron, his descendants, and every generation after them. 💧
Yahweh gave Moses another instruction: 📜
Get the finest spices: five hundred shekels of liquid myrrh, half that much—two hundred fifty shekels—of fragrant cinnamon, and two hundred fifty shekels of fragrant cane. 🌿
Also get five hundred sanctuary-shekels of cassia and one hin of olive oil. ⚖️
Have a skilled perfumer blend them into sacred anointing oil. This oil is holy. 🫙
Use it to anoint the Meeting Tent and the covenant chest. 🕊️
Anoint the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and its accessories, and the incense altar. 🕯️
Anoint the burnt-offering altar and all its tools, plus the basin and its stand. 🫙
Set these things apart so they become most holy. Whatever touches them must be treated as holy. ✨
Anoint Aaron and his sons too, setting them apart to serve me as priests. 🙏
Tell Israel: ‘This will be my sacred anointing oil for every generation. 🕊️
Don’t pour it on an ordinary person’s body or make another blend with the same recipe. It’s holy, and you must treat it as holy. 🚫
Anyone who mixes a copy of it or puts it on an outsider must be cut off from their people.’ ⚠️
Yahweh said to Moses, ‘Get sweet spices: gum resin, onycha, and galbanum, along with pure frankincense. Use equal amounts of each. 🌿
Have a perfumer blend them into incense, season it with salt, and keep it pure and holy. 🧂
Grind some of it into a fine powder and put it in front of the covenant in the Meeting Tent, where I meet with you. Treat it as most holy. 🕊️
Don’t make this incense blend for yourselves. Keep it holy for Yahweh. 🚫
Anyone who makes a copy just to enjoy its smell must be cut off from their people.’ ⚠️
Yahweh spoke to Moses: 📜
‘Look, I’ve personally chosen Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from Judah’s tribe. 👀
I’ve filled him with God’s Spirit—with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill for every kind of craft. 🧠
He can design beautiful work in gold, silver, and bronze, 🎨
cut stones for settings, carve wood, and handle every kind of skilled work. 💎
I’ve also assigned Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from Dan’s tribe, to work with him. I’ve given skill to every wise-hearted craftsperson too, so they can make everything I commanded you: 🛠️
the Meeting Tent, the covenant chest, its atonement cover, and all the Tent’s furnishings; ⛺
the table and its utensils, the pure gold lampstand and all its accessories, and the incense altar; 🕯️
the burnt-offering altar with all its utensils, plus the basin and its stand; 🫙
the finely made garments—the sacred clothes for Aaron the priest, and the clothes his sons wear while serving as priests; 👘
and the anointing oil and fragrant incense for the holy place. They must make everything just as I commanded you.’ 🫙
Yahweh spoke to Moses again: 📜
‘Tell Israel: Keep my Sabbaths. They’re a sign between me and you through every generation, so you’ll know I am Yahweh, the one who makes you holy.’ 🕊️
‘Keep the Sabbath; it’s holy to you. Anyone who treats it as ordinary must be put to death. Whoever works that day must be cut off from their people. ⚠️
‘Work six days. The seventh is a Sabbath—a day of complete rest, holy to Yahweh. Anyone who works on the Sabbath must be put to death. 🕯️
‘Israel must keep the Sabbath through every generation, honoring it as a lasting covenant. 📜
‘It’s a permanent sign between me and Israel. Yahweh made heaven and earth in six days; on the seventh day he stopped and was refreshed.’ 🌌
When Yahweh finished speaking with Moses on Mount Sinai, he gave him the two covenant tablets—stone tablets written by God’s own finger. 🪨

When the people saw Moses taking so long to come down from the mountain, they crowded around Aaron: ‘Come on, make us gods to lead us. This Moses—the guy who brought us out of Egypt—we don’t even know what happened to him.’ ⛰️
Aaron told them, ‘Take off the gold rings from your wives’, sons’, and daughters’ ears and bring them here.’ 💍
Everybody took the gold rings out of their ears and brought them to Aaron. 💍
He took the gold they handed over, shaped it with a tool, and made a calf idol. Then they said, ‘Israel, these are your gods—the ones who brought you up from Egypt.’ 🐂
When Aaron saw it, he built an altar in front of the calf. Then he announced, ‘Tomorrow we’re holding a feast for Yahweh.’ 📣
They got up early the next day, brought burnt and peace offerings, then sat down to eat and drink. After that, they got up to celebrate. 🍽️
Yahweh told Moses, ‘Go down there. Your people—the ones you brought out of Egypt—have gone way off track! ⚠️
‘They ditched my instructions almost immediately. They made a metal calf, bowed to it, offered sacrifices to it, and said, “Israel, these are your gods who brought you up from Egypt.”’ 🐂
Yahweh told Moses, ‘I’ve seen these people. They’re stubborn, for real. 😠
‘Leave me alone so my anger can burn against them and wipe them out. Then I’ll make a great nation from you.’ 🔥
Moses pleaded with Yahweh his God: ‘Yahweh, why let your anger burn against your own people? You brought them out of Egypt with huge power and a mighty hand. 🙏

‘Why give the Egyptians a chance to say, “He brought them out just to kill them in the mountains and wipe them off the earth”? Turn back from this fierce anger; don’t bring this disaster on your people. 🗣️
‘Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, your servants. You swore by yourself: “I’ll make your descendants as many as the stars, and I’ll give them all this land I promised; they’ll keep it forever.”’ ✨
So Yahweh held back from bringing the disaster he had said would come on his people. 🕊️
Moses turned and headed down the mountain with the two covenant tablets in his hands. Writing covered both sides—front and back. 🪨
God had made the tablets, and God’s own writing was engraved on them. ✍️
Joshua heard the people shouting and said to Moses, ‘That sounds like fighting in the camp.’ 👂
Moses replied, ‘That’s not a victory shout, and it’s not a cry of defeat either. I hear singing.’ 🎶
As soon as Moses got near the camp and saw the calf and dancing, his anger flared. He threw the tablets from his hands and smashed them at the foot of the mountain. 💥
He took the calf they had made, burned it, ground it into powder, scattered it on the water, and made Israel drink it. 🐂
Moses challenged Aaron: ‘What did these people do to you, that you’ve brought such a serious sin on them?’ 🗣️
Aaron said, ‘Please don’t be angry with me, sir. You know these people—they’re set on doing wrong. 😰
‘They told me, “Make gods to lead us. We don’t know what happened to Moses, the man who brought us out of Egypt.” 🗣️
‘So I told them, “Whoever has gold, take it off.” They gave it to me; I tossed it into the fire—and out came this calf.’ 🐂
Moses saw the people had lost all control. Aaron had let them run wild, leaving them exposed to their enemies’ ridicule. 😔
Moses stood at the camp entrance and called out, ‘Whoever is on Yahweh’s side, come over to me!’ All the Levites gathered around him. 📣
He told them, ‘Yahweh, Israel’s God, says: “Each man, strap on your sword. Go through the camp from entrance to entrance; each of you must kill his brother, friend, and neighbor.”’ ⚔️
The Levites did what Moses commanded. About three thousand people died that day. 🕯️
Moses said, ‘Today you’ve set yourselves apart for Yahweh, even at the cost of turning against son or brother. May he give you a blessing today.’ 🙏
The next day Moses told the people, ‘You’ve committed a huge sin. Now I’m going up to Yahweh. Maybe I can make atonement for your sin.’ 🕊️
Moses went back to Yahweh and said, ‘Oh, these people have committed a huge sin. They made gods out of gold. 😔
‘But please forgive their sin. If you won’t, erase me from the book you’ve written.’ 🙏
Yahweh replied to Moses, ‘I’ll erase from my book whoever sins against me. 📜
‘Now go lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel will go ahead of you. But when the time comes to punish, I’ll hold them accountable for their sin.’ 🕊️
Yahweh struck the people because they had made the calf—the one Aaron made. ⚠️
Yahweh told Moses, ‘Move out from here—you and the people you brought up from Egypt. Head to the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, the land I swore to give their descendants. 🧭
‘I’ll send an angel ahead of you. I’ll drive out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites. 🕊️
‘Go to a land flowing with milk and honey. But I won’t travel among you, because you’re stubborn. I might destroy you on the way.’ ⚠️
When the people heard this hard news, they mourned, and no one put on their jewelry. 😔
Yahweh had told Moses, ‘Tell Israel: “You’re stubborn people. If I traveled among you even for a moment, I could destroy you. Now take off your jewelry, and I’ll decide what to do with you.”’ 📿
So, from Mount Horeb onward, the Israelites left their jewelry off. 📿
Moses would take a tent and pitch it far outside the camp. He called it the Meeting Tent. Anyone seeking Yahweh went out there, beyond the camp. ⛺
Whenever Moses headed to the Tent, everyone stood at their own tent entrance and watched until he went inside. 👀
When Moses entered, the cloud pillar came down and stood at the Tent’s entrance while Yahweh spoke with him. ☁️
Everyone saw the cloud pillar at the entrance. Then they stood up and worshiped, each person at their own tent doorway. 🙏
Yahweh spoke with Moses face to face, like one person talking with a friend. Then Moses returned to camp, but his young assistant Joshua son of Nun stayed at the Tent. 🤝
Moses said to Yahweh, ‘You told me, “Lead these people,” but you haven’t said who’ll come with me. You also told me, “I know you by name, and you have my favor.” 🙏
‘So if I really have your favor, please show me your way. Help me know you, so I can keep your favor. Remember too: this nation is your people.’ 🧭
Yahweh replied, ‘I’ll go with you, and I’ll give you rest.’ 🕊️
Moses said, ‘If you don’t go with us, don’t make us leave this place. 🙏
‘How will anyone know I have your favor—me and your people—unless you go with us? That’s what sets us apart from every other people on earth.’ 🌍
Yahweh told Moses, ‘I’ll do what you’ve asked. You have my favor, and I know you by name.’ 🕊️
Moses said, ‘Please show me your glory.’ ✨
Yahweh answered, ‘I’ll let all my goodness pass in front of you, and I’ll announce my name, Yahweh. I show grace to whoever I choose, and mercy to whoever I choose.’ 🕊️
He said, ‘You can’t see my face; no human can see me and live.’ ⚠️
Yahweh continued, ‘There’s a spot beside me. Stand on that rock. 🪨
‘When my glory passes by, I’ll put you in a crack in the rock and cover you with my hand until I’ve passed. ✋
‘Then I’ll move my hand, and you’ll see my back—but my face won’t be seen.’ 🕊️
Yahweh told Moses, “Chisel two stone tablets like the first ones. I’ll write on them the words from the tablets you broke. 🪨
Be ready first thing in the morning. Hike up Mount Sinai and meet me at the top. ⛰️
No one may come up with you or be seen anywhere on the mountain. Don’t let the flocks or herds graze in front of it.” 🐑
Moses cut two stone tablets like the first ones. He got up at dawn, climbed Sinai just as Yahweh said, and carried both tablets with him. 🌄
Yahweh came down in the cloud, stood with Moses, and proclaimed his name. ☁️
Yahweh passed in front of Moses and called out: “Yahweh! Yahweh! A compassionate, gracious God—slow to anger, overflowing with faithful love and truth, 🕊️

showing faithful love to thousands, forgiving wrongdoing, rebellion, and sin—yet never calling the guilty innocent. He holds parents’ wrongdoing to account through the third and fourth generations.” ⚖️
Moses quickly bowed low to the ground and worshiped. 🙏
He said, “Lord, if I have your favor, please stay among us. Yeah, these people are stubborn, but forgive our wrongdoing and sin, and claim us as your own.” 🕊️
Yahweh said, “Here’s the covenant: in front of all your people, I’ll do wonders nobody has seen anywhere on earth or among any nation. Everyone with you will see my work—it’ll leave them in awe. ✨
“Lock in on what I’m commanding you today. I’ll drive out the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites ahead of you. 🗺️
“Stay sharp: don’t make a covenant with the people in the land you’re entering. That deal could turn into a trap for you. ⚠️
“Tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, and cut down their Asherah poles. 🪓
“Don’t worship any other god. My name is Jealous; I am a jealous God. 🙏
“Don’t make a covenant with the people of the land. They may be unfaithful by chasing their gods, sacrificing to them, and inviting you to eat from those sacrifices. ⚠️
Your sons might marry their daughters, and those daughters may chase their gods and draw your sons into doing the same. 💍
“Don’t make any cast-metal gods for yourselves. 🚫
“Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Eat unleavened bread for seven days at the set time in Abib, just as I commanded—you came out of Egypt in that month. 🍞
“Every firstborn belongs to me, including the firstborn males of your cattle and sheep. 🐑
Redeem a firstborn donkey with a lamb; if you don’t redeem it, break its neck. Redeem every firstborn son. No one may come before me empty-handed. 🐴
“Work six days, then rest on the seventh—even when it’s plowing season or harvest time. 🌾
“Keep the Feast of Weeks with the first wheat harvest, and the Feast of Ingathering when the year wraps up. 🌾
“Three times a year, every male must show up before Lord Yahweh, Israel’s God. 🙏
“I’ll drive nations out ahead of you and widen your borders. When you travel to appear before Yahweh your God those three times a year, no one will try to take your land. 🛡️
“Don’t offer the blood of my sacrifice with leavened bread. Don’t leave any of the Passover sacrifice until morning. 🌙
“Bring the first of the firstfruits from your land to the house of Yahweh your God. Don’t boil a young goat in its mother’s milk.” 🌱
Yahweh told Moses, “Write down these words. I have made a covenant with you and Israel based on them.” ✍️
Moses stayed there with Yahweh forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water. He wrote the covenant words—the Ten Commandments—on the tablets. ⏳
When Moses came down Mount Sinai with the two covenant tablets in his hands, he didn’t know that his face was shining because he had spoken with Yahweh. ✨
Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses’ shining face and were afraid to come near him. 😨
Moses called to them. Aaron and all the community’s leaders came back, and Moses spoke with them. 🗣️
After that, all the Israelites came near, and Moses gave them every command Yahweh had spoken to him on Mount Sinai. 📜
When Moses finished speaking, he put a veil over his face. 🧕
Whenever Moses went in before Yahweh to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out. Then he told the Israelites what Yahweh had commanded. 🙏
The Israelites saw that Moses’ face was shining, so he put the veil over his face again until he went in to speak with Yahweh. ✨
Moses gathered the whole Israelite community and said, ‘Here’s what Yahweh commanded you to do: 📣
‘Work for six days, but the seventh day is sacred—a Sabbath of complete rest for Yahweh. Anyone who works that day must be put to death. 🕯️
‘Don’t even light a fire in your homes on the Sabbath.’ 🔥
Moses told the whole Israelite community, ‘This is what Yahweh commanded: 📜
‘Bring Yahweh an offering from among your people. Whoever truly wants to give can bring gold, silver, or bronze. 💛
‘Bring blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, or goat hair; 🧶
‘ram skins dyed red, sea-cow hides, or acacia wood; 🪵
‘oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil and fragrant incense; 🪔
‘and onyx stones plus gems to set in the ephod and chest piece. 💎
‘Let every skilled craftsperson among you come through and make everything Yahweh commanded: 🛠️
‘the Meeting Tent with its coverings, roof, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases; ⛺
‘the covenant chest and its poles, the atonement cover, and the curtain; 🪨
‘the table, its poles and utensils, and the bread of the Presence; 🍞
‘the lampstand for light, its accessories, its lamps, and the oil; 🕯️
‘the incense altar with its poles, the anointing oil, fragrant incense, and the entrance curtain for the Tent; 🫙
‘the burnt-offering altar, its bronze grating, poles and tools, and the basin with its stand; 🫙
‘the courtyard curtains, posts and bases, and the screen for the courtyard gate; 🚪
‘the Tent and courtyard pegs, plus their ropes; 🪢
‘and the finely made service clothes for the holy place—the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments his sons wear as priests.’ 👘
Then the whole Israelite community left Moses. 🚶
Everyone who felt moved to give, and everyone whose heart was willing, brought an offering for the Meeting Tent, all its service, and the sacred garments. 🙌
Men and women came forward—everyone willing to give. They brought brooches, earrings, signet rings, armlets, and all kinds of gold jewelry. Each person presented their gold to Yahweh. 💍
Anyone who had blue, purple, or scarlet yarn, fine linen, goat hair, red-dyed ram skins, or sea-cow hides brought it along. 🧵
Everyone willing to give silver or bronze brought it as Yahweh’s offering. Those with acacia wood for the work brought that too. 🪙
All the skilled women spun yarn by hand and brought what they made: blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen. 🧶
The women whose hearts moved them, and who had the skill, spun goat hair. 🧶
The leaders brought onyx stones and gems for the ephod and chest piece, 💎
‘along with spices and oil for the lamps, the anointing oil, and the fragrant incense. 🪔
Every Israelite man and woman whose heart was willing brought a freewill offering to Yahweh for all the work he had commanded Moses to have done. 🙌
Moses told the Israelites, ‘Look, Yahweh has personally chosen Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from Judah’s tribe. 👀
‘He has filled him with God’s Spirit—with wisdom, understanding, knowledge, and skill for every kind of craft; 🧠
‘he can design fine work and shape gold, silver, and bronze; 🎨
‘cut gems for settings, carve wood, and handle every kind of skilled craft. 🪵
‘God has also put it in his heart to teach—him and Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from Dan’s tribe. 📚
‘He has equipped them with wisdom to do every kind of craft: engraving, skilled design, embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, weaving, and all kinds of expert work.’ 🧵
Bezalel, Oholiab, and every skilled craftsperson must do the work just as Yahweh commanded—with the wisdom and understanding he gave them for serving in the holy place. 🛠️
Moses called Bezalel, Oholiab, and every craftsperson whose heart Yahweh had made wise, everyone moved to come do the work. 📣
They received from Moses all the offerings Israel had brought for the holy-place work. People kept bringing freewill gifts every morning. 🌅
Then all the skilled workers making the holy place paused their work and came over to Moses. 🛠️
They told him, ‘The people have brought way more than enough for the work Yahweh told us to do!’ 🙌
Moses sent word through the camp: ‘No more gifts from men or women for the holy place.’ So the people stopped bringing them. 📣
They already had enough supplies for all the work—and then some. 📦
The skilled workers made the Meeting Tent from ten curtains of finely woven linen, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, with cherubim woven into them. 🧵
Each curtain was twenty-eight cubits long and four cubits wide. All ten had the same measurements. 📏
They joined five curtains together as one set, then joined the other five into a second set. 🪡
They made blue loops along the edge of the outer curtain in the first set, and did the same on the edge of the outer curtain in the second set. 🔵
Each of those two curtain edges got fifty loops, lined up opposite one another. 〰️
They made fifty gold clasps and fastened the sets together. Just like that, the Tent became one piece. ✨
They made eleven goat-hair curtains to cover the Tent. 🐐
Each curtain was thirty cubits long and four cubits wide. All eleven were the same size. 📏
They joined five curtains as one set and six as another. 🧵
They put fifty loops along the outer edge of each set, matching them up across from one another. 〰️
They made fifty bronze clasps to fasten the tent covering into one piece. 🟤
They added a covering of ram skins dyed red, with a sea-cow hide covering above it. 🐏
They made upright frames for the Tent from acacia wood. 🪵
Each frame was ten cubits long and one and a half cubits wide. 📐
Each frame had two matching pegs joined together. They made every Tent frame this way. 🪵
For the south side of the Tent, they made twenty frames. 🧭
They made forty silver bases under those twenty frames—two bases for each frame, one under each peg. 🪙
For the north side, they also made twenty frames, 🧭
with forty silver bases: two under each frame. 🪙
For the back of the Tent, facing west, they made six frames. 🧭
They made two more frames for the Tent’s back corners. 🪵
Those corner frames were doubled at the bottom and joined at the top with one ring. They did this for both corners. 🔗
That made eight frames with sixteen silver bases—two bases under every frame. 🔢
They made acacia crossbars: five for the frames on one side of the Tent, 🪵
five for the other side, and five for the back, facing west. 🪵
They made the middle crossbar run straight through the center of the frames from one end to the other. ➖
They covered the frames with gold, made gold rings to hold the crossbars, and covered the bars with gold too. ✨
They made the veil from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely woven linen, with cherubim woven in by a skilled craftsperson. 🧵
They made four acacia posts for the veil and covered them with gold. Their hooks were gold too, and they cast four silver bases for them. 🪙
They made an embroidered entrance screen for the Tent from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely woven linen. 🧵
They made five posts for it, with hooks. They covered the capitals and connecting bands with gold, and made five bronze bases. ✨
Bezalel made the covenant chest from acacia wood: two and a half cubits long, one and a half wide, and one and a half tall. 🪵
He covered it inside and out with pure gold, then added a gold border all around. ✨
He cast four gold rings for its feet—two on one side and two on the other. 💍
He made carrying poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold. 🪵
He slid the poles through the rings on the chest’s sides so it could be carried. 📦
He made the atonement cover from pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide. ✨
He hammered out two gold cherubim, placing one at each end of the atonement cover. 👼
There was one cherub at each end, shaped as one piece with the cover. 🪽
Their wings stretched over the cover, shading it. The cherubim faced one another, looking down toward the cover. 🪽
He made the table from acacia wood: two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits tall. 🪵
He covered it with pure gold and put a gold border around it. ✨
He added a rim one handbreadth wide around the table, then put a gold border around the rim. 📏
He cast four gold rings and attached them to the four corners at the table’s legs. 💍
The rings sat right beside the rim, ready to hold the poles for carrying the table. 🪙
He made those carrying poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold. 🪵
He made all the table’s utensils from pure gold: dishes, spoons, bowls, and pitchers for pouring. 🍶
He made the lampstand from pure gold, hammering it into one piece with its base, stem, cups, buds, and flowers. 🕯️
Six branches came out from its sides—three on one side and three on the other. 🌿
Each branch had three cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and flowers. All six branches had the same design. 🌸
On the lampstand itself were four cups shaped like almond blossoms, with their buds and flowers. 🌸
There was one bud under each pair of branches—three buds total for the six branches growing from the stand. 🌱
The buds and branches were all part of the same piece. The whole lampstand was one hammered work of pure gold. ✨
He made its seven lamps, wick trimmers, and ash trays from pure gold. 🕯️
The lampstand and all its utensils used one talent of pure gold. ⚖️
He made the incense altar from acacia wood. It was square—one cubit long, one cubit wide, and two cubits tall—with horns shaped as one piece. 🪵
He covered the top, sides, and horns with pure gold and put a gold border around it. ✨
He made two gold rings under the border, one on each side, to hold the poles for carrying the altar. 💍
He made the carrying poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold. 🪵
He made the sacred anointing oil and pure, fragrant incense—the work of a skilled perfumer. 🌿
He built the burnt-offering altar from acacia wood, five cubits long and wide and three cubits tall. 📐
He shaped a horn at each of its four corners as one piece with the altar, then covered it with bronze. 🟤
He made all the altar gear from bronze: pots, shovels, bowls, forks, and fire pans. 🛠️
He made a bronze mesh grate for the altar, set beneath its rim and reaching halfway up. 🔥
He cast four bronze rings at the grate’s four corners to hold the carrying poles. 💍
He made the poles from acacia wood and covered them with bronze. 🪵
He slid the poles through the altar’s side rings so it could be carried. The altar itself was hollow, made from boards. 📦
He made the bronze basin and its stand from mirrors donated by the women who served at the entrance of the Meeting Tent. 🪞
Then he set up the courtyard. On its south side, the linen curtains stretched one hundred cubits. 🧵
That side had twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, with silver hooks and connecting bands. 🪙
The north side was also one hundred cubits long, with twenty posts and twenty bronze bases, plus silver hooks and bands. 🧭
The west side had fifty cubits of curtains, ten posts, and ten bases. Its post hooks and bands were silver. 🧭
The east side, facing the sunrise, was fifty cubits across. 🌅
On one side of the entrance were fifteen cubits of curtains, three posts, and three bases; 🚪
the other side matched: fifteen cubits of curtains, three posts, and three bases. 🚪
Every curtain around the courtyard was made from finely woven linen. 🧵
The post bases were bronze; the hooks and bands were silver. The post tops were covered in silver, and every courtyard post had a silver band. ✨
The courtyard gate screen was embroidered in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely woven linen. It was twenty cubits long and five cubits high, matching the courtyard curtains. 🧵
It had four posts with four bronze bases, silver hooks, and silver coverings on their tops and bands. 🪙
Every Tent peg and every peg around the courtyard was bronze. 🔩
Here’s the inventory of materials used for the Meeting Tent—the Tent of the Covenant. Moses ordered the count for the Levites’ service, and Ithamar son of Aaron the priest supervised it. 📋
Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from Judah’s tribe, made everything Yahweh commanded Moses. 🛠️
Oholiab son of Ahisamach, from Dan’s tribe, worked alongside him. He was an engraver, a skilled craftsperson, and an embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen. 🎨
The gold used for all the sanctuary work—including the people’s offering—weighed twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty sanctuary-shekels. ⚖️
The silver from the community’s census weighed one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five sanctuary-shekels. 🪙
Each person counted, twenty years old or older, gave one bekah—half a sanctuary-shekel. That was collected from 603,550 men. 🔢
The one hundred talents of silver were cast into bases for the sanctuary and the veil: one hundred bases total, one talent of silver for each base. 🪙
From the remaining one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, he made the post hooks, covered their tops, and made their silver bands. ⚒️
The bronze offering weighed seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels. ⚖️
With it he made the Meeting Tent entrance bases, the bronze altar and its grate, and all the altar’s tools; 🛠️
the bases around the courtyard and at its gate, plus every Tent peg and every peg around the courtyard. 📋
They used blue, purple, and scarlet yarn to make the sacred service clothes and garments for Aaron—just as Yahweh commanded Moses. 👘
They made the ephod from gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, plus finely woven linen. ✨
They hammered gold into thin sheets, cut it into fine threads, and worked it into the blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and linen—the work of a skilled craftsperson. 🧵
They made two shoulder straps for the ephod, joining it together at both ends. 🪡
The ephod’s woven waistband matched it: one piece made from gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen, exactly as Yahweh commanded Moses. 🪢
They set the onyx stones in gold settings and engraved them like signet seals with Israel’s sons’ names. 💎
They put the stones on the ephod’s shoulder straps as a memorial for Israel—just as Yahweh commanded Moses. 🪨
They made the chest piece with the same skilled work and materials as the ephod: gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and fine linen. 👘
They folded it double into a square, one span long and one span wide. 📐
They set four rows of gems in it. First row: ruby, topaz, and beryl. 💎
Second row: turquoise, sapphire, and emerald. 💎
Third row: jacinth, agate, and amethyst. 💎
Fourth row: chrysolite, onyx, and jasper, all held in gold settings. ✨
There were twelve stones, one for each of Israel’s tribes, engraved like a signet with each tribe’s name. 🔢
They made braided gold chains for the chest piece. ⛓️
They made two gold settings and two gold rings, then attached one ring to each end of the chest piece. 💍
They threaded the two braided gold chains through the rings at the chest piece’s ends. ⛓️
They attached the chains’ other ends to the two settings on the front of the ephod’s shoulder straps. 🪢
They made two more gold rings and attached them to the chest piece’s inner lower edges beside the ephod. 💍
They made two more gold rings for the front of the ephod’s shoulder straps, just below the join and above its woven waistband. 💍
They tied the chest piece’s rings to the ephod’s rings with blue cord, so it stayed secured to the waistband—just as Yahweh commanded Moses. 🔵
They made the ephod’s robe entirely from blue woven cloth. 🔵
It had an opening in the middle, finished like a collar, so it wouldn’t tear. 👘
Around the robe’s hem they made pomegranates from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely twisted linen. 🔴
They made pure-gold bells and placed them around the hem between the pomegranates. 🔔
The hem alternated bell, pomegranate, bell, pomegranate all around, for priestly service—just as Yahweh commanded Moses. 🔔
They wove fine-linen tunics for Aaron and his sons, 👕
plus the fine-linen turban, headbands, and undergarments; 🧵
and an embroidered sash of fine linen and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn—just as Yahweh commanded Moses. 🪡
They made the sacred crown’s plate from pure gold and engraved it like a signet: “HOLY TO YAHWEH.” 👑
They tied a blue cord to it and fastened it to the front of the turban, just as Yahweh commanded Moses. 🔵
That’s how all the Meeting Tent’s work was completed. Israel did everything Yahweh commanded Moses—they got it all done. ✅
They brought the whole Tent to Moses: the tent and all its furnishings, clasps, frames, bars, posts, and bases; 📦
the red-dyed ram-skin covering, the sea-cow hide covering, and the curtain; 🐏
the covenant chest with its poles and the atonement cover; 🪨
the table, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence; 🍞
the pure-gold lampstand, its lamps arranged in order, all its accessories, and the lamp oil; 🕯️
the gold altar, anointing oil, fragrant incense, and the Tent’s entrance screen; 🫙
the bronze altar, its grate, poles and utensils, and the basin with its stand; 🟤
the courtyard curtains, posts and bases, the gate screen, ropes, pegs, and every tool used in the Tent’s service; 📋
the finely made service clothes for the holy place—the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and the garments his sons wore as priests. 👘
Israel had done all the work exactly as Yahweh commanded Moses. ✅
Moses inspected everything. They had made it just as Yahweh commanded, and Moses blessed them. 🙌
Yahweh told Moses: 📜
‘On the first day of the first month, set up the Meeting Tent—the Dwelling. ⛺
‘Put the covenant chest inside and hide it behind the curtain. 🪨
‘Bring in the table and arrange everything on it. Bring in the lampstand and light its lamps. 🕯️
‘Place the gold incense altar in front of the covenant chest, then hang the Tent’s entrance screen. ✨
‘Set the burnt-offering altar at the entrance to the Meeting Tent. 🔥
‘Put the basin between the Tent and altar, and fill it with water. 🚰
‘Set up the courtyard around the Tent and hang its gate screen. 🚪
‘Take the anointing oil and anoint the Tent and everything inside it. Set the Tent and all its furnishings apart as holy. 🫙
‘Anoint the burnt-offering altar and all its tools; set the altar apart, and it will be most holy. 🕊️
‘Anoint the basin and its stand too, setting them apart. 💧
‘Bring Aaron and his sons to the Meeting Tent entrance and wash them with water. 💧
‘Dress Aaron in the sacred garments, anoint him, and set him apart to serve me as a priest. 👘
‘Bring his sons too and put tunics on them. 👕
‘Anoint them just as you anointed their father, so they can serve me as priests. Their anointing establishes a lasting priesthood for every generation.’ 🕊️
Moses did exactly what Yahweh commanded him. ✅
In the first month of the second year, on the first day, the Meeting Tent was set up. 🗓️
Moses set up the Tent, laid its bases, stood up its frames, slid in the crossbars, and raised its posts. ⛺
He spread the covering over the Tent and placed the roof on top, just as Yahweh commanded him. 🏕️
He placed the covenant tablets inside the chest, set the poles in place, and put the atonement cover on top. 🪨
He carried the chest into the Tent, hung the curtain, and screened off the covenant chest, just as Yahweh commanded him. 🪟
He put the table in the Meeting Tent on the north side, outside the curtain, 📋
and arranged the bread on it before Yahweh, just as Yahweh commanded him. 🍞
He put the lampstand in the Meeting Tent across from the table, on the Tent’s south side. 🕯️
He lit the lamps before Yahweh, just as Yahweh commanded him. 🔥
He placed the gold altar inside the Meeting Tent, in front of the curtain, ✨
and burned fragrant incense on it, just as Yahweh commanded him. 🌿
He hung the screen at the Tent’s entrance. 🚪
He set the burnt-offering altar at the entrance to the Meeting Tent and offered the burnt and grain offerings there, just as Yahweh commanded him. 🔥
He put the basin between the Meeting Tent and the altar and filled it with water for washing. 💧
Moses, Aaron, and Aaron’s sons washed their hands and feet there. 🧼
They washed whenever they entered the Meeting Tent or came near the altar, exactly as Yahweh had commanded Moses. 💧
Moses raised the courtyard around the Tent and altar and set up the gate screen. That wrapped up the work. ✅
Then the cloud covered the Meeting Tent, and Yahweh’s glory filled the Dwelling. ☁️
Moses couldn’t enter the Meeting Tent because the cloud rested over it and Yahweh’s glory filled the Dwelling. ✨
Whenever the cloud lifted from above the Dwelling, the Israelites would pack up and move on through their journeys. 🧭
But if the cloud stayed put, they stayed too, waiting until the day it lifted. ⏳
Yahweh’s cloud stayed over the Dwelling by day, and fire glowed inside it at night, in full view of all Israel throughout every journey. 🔥
